To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human stomach tumor cells were the most sensitive of three types of cells studied to the killing action of diaziquone; that the killing action of AZQ was greatest in the G2 and late S/G2 phases of the CHO cell cycle; and that even at non-cytotoxic concentrations of AZQ, CHO cells were blocked in the S and/or G2 phases of their cell cycle.

AZQ is a highly selective anticancer drug that is more effective against dividing than nondividing cells, that it is more effective against cells in the late S/G _{2} phase than cells in the early S, G _{1} or G _{2} phases, and that it can be used in combination with other drugs to increase the effectiveness against tumors.

AZQ is more effective against nondividing CHO and human tumor cells than against dividing CHO cells, that the sensitivity of CHO cells to AZQ killing is greatest at the late S-G2 phase boundary, and that AZQ causes large, but reversible, enrichments of CHO cells in the S- and G2-phases of the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the antitumor agent diaziquone.
the study of cell cycle kinetics and survival effects of the anticancer drug diaziquone, AZQ (NSC 18686) on three different cell lines in vitro.
the effects of a new anticancer drug on three cell types in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AZQ is a very potent antitumor agent with a high degree of cell cycle specificity.
the cytotoxicity of AZQ is related to both cell cycle stage sensitivity and cell cycle kinetics.
AZQ has a unique spectrum of effects on the cell cycle and cell cycle kinetics of CHO cells, and clones from human astrocytoma and stomach tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cell killing effect of AZQ is dependent on the cell cycle stage at which the cells are exposed to AZQ, and that AZQ can cause reversible cell cycle stage-dependent perturbations in the cell cycle kinetics of exponentially growing CHO cells.
the cytotoxicity and cell cycle effects of AZQ are very complex.

AZQ is a potent agent for treating a variety of human cancers, but that the drug is most effective in treating those tumors that have a high proportion of dividing cells and that have a large number of cells in late S/G2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AZQ's cell cycle kinetics effects on cells are very similar to those of other alkylating agents such as nitrogen mustard, and that the drug's effects are most pronounced in nondividing cells.
